blocks.text: Best Biohacking Books For Beginners

We want to start our journey from the basic famous books for [beginners in biohacking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-for-beginners). These are the perfect publications to discover more about wellness and body power.
1. “LIFESPAN: WHY WE AGE AND WHY WE DON’T HAVE TO” \ DAVID SINCLAIR
Would you take health and beauty advice from a 50-year-old who looks 20 years younger? If so, then you definitely need to read this biohacking book.

David Sinclair, a professor at Harvard Medical School and a researcher of the molecular mechanisms of aging, published Lifespan: Why We Age and Why We Don’t Have to, where he explained in detail [why we age, how to measure this process, and how to slow it down](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-biohacking-can-reverse-aging).
The book was published two years ago when the World Health Organization added aging to the register of diseases. Yes, you heard right — it turns out to be a disease!

The author debunks the theory that aging is caused by the loss of genetic information (spoiler: it’s all about epigenetics). He also discusses experiments accelerating aging in certain parts of the body and how a machine learning algorithm can predict your biological age based on the number of methyl groups on cytosine in your DNA.

This biohacking book offers [practical advice on improving sleep quality](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-sleep), body mass index, whether to skip lunch breaks and the benefits of taking the stairs and [exercising](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/fitness-and-biohacking) regularly.

You will also learn about exciting studies and experiments showing that the body can be made old, not entirely, but only in certain places. One of the best-selling comments in the book is a YouTube user’s review under Sinclair’s lecture on Google: “A man who looks 30 at 50 gives advice about aging? I’m all ears.”
2. Head Strong: The Bulletproof Plan to Activate Untapped Brain Energy to Work Smarter and Think Faster-in Just Two Weeks \  DAVE ASPREY

Suppose you are constantly tired or feel a loss of energy every day at a particular time. In that case, [brain biohacking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-to-biohack-brain-health) is something you need to pay attention to. In this biohacker`s handbook, you will learn how to get the energy you need by changing your environment and turning off external stimuli that are harmful to your brain.
Dave Asprey is a Silicon Valley investor and founder of the Bulletproof Executive blog, read by about 1.5 million visitors monthly. He also has his own podcast, which has millions of downloads.

At one time, Dave spent 15 years of his life and $300 thousand to thoroughly and meticulously study biohacking and the human brain’s capabilities. His efforts were worthwhile. Thanks to his research, Dave [lost weight without exhausting calorie counting](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-for-weight-loss), raised his IQ by several points, learned to get enough sleep quickly, and reduced his biological age. Lately we will focus exactly on Dave Asprey biohacking book.
3. Sleep Smarter by Shawn Stevenson

Do you like to lie in bed “to the last”? Who doesn’t! All sleepyheads will definitely enjoy this biohacking book! But are you sure you spend enough time sleeping? Is it possible to improve the quality of your sleep? And if so, how do you do it right? Even if you swear that you follow all the rules of healthy sleep, you will find unexpected discoveries in the book.

4. Brain Body Diet by Sara Gottfried

Want to learn tips from the personal physicians of many Hollywood celebrities? Then, be sure to read Sarah Gottfried’s biohacking book! It is written specifically [for women](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-for-women).

The preventive medicine and gynecologist doctor will share the basic principles to help you [stay young and beautiful](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-skincare), lose weight, and harmonize your body and mind.

Her course will especially appeal to those who like quick results, as it lasts for 40 days. During this time, you’ll improve yourself in eight areas. And before that, you can assess your progress in each of them. If you want to feel what the stars do to look amazing, go ahead!
5. Biohacker’s Handbook: Upgrade yourself and unleash your inner potential \ JAAKKO HALMETOJA, OLLI SOVIJÄRVI, TEEMU ARINA

According to the book’s authors, practicing physician Olli Soviarvi, digitalization specialist Teemu Arina, and nutrition expert Jaakko Halmetoja believe preventing a disease is better than treating it.

In their book, biohackers explore the human body and study how each system works. The biohacking book can be considered a reference book because it contains many simple, functional, practical recommendations and the most up-to-date research in physiology, genetics, and biochemistry.

You will also find many tables and graphs. This biohackers handbook covers the most critical issues, including why improving sleep quality is essential, what food is physiologically optimal, and how to choose the proper daily routine.
Biohacking Books For Advanced Biohackers
Mitochondria and the Future of Medicine: The Key to Understanding Disease, Lee Know

A licensed naturopathic doctor from Canada, Lee Noe talks in simple terms about serious diseases: cancer, myocardial infarction, stroke, and Alzheimer’s disease. Readers will learn about the causes and interrelationships between these dangerous ailments.

According to the doctor, most of them are common, which means that fighting serious diseases is easier than it may seem at first glance. All it takes is to restore the health of mitochondria, tiny organelles on which the body depends much more than is commonly believed.
Despite the complex and voluminous topic and abundant chemical terms in the first chapters, this biohacking book reads very quickly.
The Feeling of Life Itself, Christoph Koch

Christoph Koch is a neuroscientist who began studying consciousness at the very dawn of the discipline and is president of the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle. He was one of the last to work with Francis Crick, who, in tandem with James Watson, discovered the structure of the DNA double helix before retraining as a neuroscientist in the late ’70s. In one of his biohacking books, Koch said Crick adopted him as his “intellectual progeny.”

Koch has been searching for the grounding of consciousness in neural structures for several decades. He often says that the lack of a clear definition of consciousness and existing attempts to provide one are reminiscent of the Buddhist parable of the blind men trying to describe the elephant. In his new book, Koch defines consciousness unambiguously once and for all — as “any subjective experience, from the simplest to the most sublime — the feeling of being alive.” He explains much about neuroscience and how to derive a measure of awareness.

Koch’s research is relevant to attempts to create artificial general intelligence (AGI). In interviews, he often says whether a machine with AGI would have consciousness is unclear. Koch also emphasizes that simulated intelligence does not equal the possibility of having conscious experiences. Suppose we are going to make machines with consciousness. In that case, it should only be neuromorphic after we understand almost everything about the human brain.
Biohacker’s Handbook

Biohacker’s Handbook is the decade’s most anticipated health & wellness book. Authors M.D. Olli Sovijärvi, technology expert Teemu Arina, and nutrition expert Jaakko Halmetoja upgrade the fundamentals of a balanced life: sleep, nutrition, exercise, work, and the mind. What is the 20 % that will lead to 80 % of the results regarding optimal well-being?
Biohackers believe that it is cheaper and more profitable to promote health than to treat disease.

The human body is made up of many different systems, and biohacking allows us to understand how these systems work. The authors talk in an accessible way about one of our century’s most promising and controversial topics. The theory, based on the authors’ work and analysis of research results, is supported by a wealth of simple, practical recommendations.
What will the book be useful for?

items: It tells about how to optimize the body’s performance through science and technology, as well as an understanding of physiology and the principles of good nutrition.
Helps to improve health, well-being, and quality of life.
Known to biohackers around the world and proven in practice.

blocks.text: Biohack Your Brain By Dave Asprey Review

For a decade, Silicon Valley entrepreneur Dave Asprey has worked with world-renowned doctors and scientists to discover what best practices can help people be more productive. This process is called “biohacking.” In his book, the author shares how you can use it to make your brain smarter, sharper, and faster.

Imagine your mind is clear, your thinking is sharp, and you can do more simultaneously. The most difficult things become amenable to you. You are 100% confident in your intelligence and don’t feel like the dumbest person in the room. You don’t worry about constantly forgetting something important. You are no longer unaware of mood swings, temper tantrums, or reaching for a sugary snack during the day.

Dave Asprey’s biohacking book will convince you that this — and much more — is possible. By changing your behavior with his life hacks, you can tap into the knowledge of how your brain works and take it to the next level.
The program in this book will help you:

items: provide your brain with precisely the food it needs to be as productive as possible throughout the day;
energize your brain’s cellular batteries — the mitochondria — to eliminate the urge to snack constantly and for total concentration;
stimulate neuronal growth to speed up brain function and learning processes.

blocks.text: You’ll learn what to eat and avoid, how to incorporate the suitable types of physical activity into your routine, workspace organization, [supplements](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/best-biohacking-supplements), detox for your home and body, and [meditation](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-meditation) and breathing practices to help you work at 100%.

blocks.text: About the author

Dave Asprey is a Silicon Valley investor, creator of the Bulletproof Executive blog (1.5 million visitors per month), and a podcast with millions of downloads, who has spent 15 years and 300,000 dollars researching the topic of biohacking and developing brain power. Thanks to the research he describes in the book, he has been able to lose serious weight without calorie counting, raise his IQ by several dozen points, get more sleep in less time, and lower his biological age.
How did we select these books
All the publications are the best in the biohacking area. We carefully curated this list of books for you based on the following criteria:

items: **Scientific foundation** — The authors have a background in medicine, biology, or related sciences, and their claims are backed by credible research.
**Recognition in the professional community** — The books are cited or recommended by experts, appear in scientific articles, or are referenced in lectures and studies.
**Popularity in the biohacking world** — The authors are well-known figures in the biohacking community, often running podcasts, blogs, or speaking at significant events.

blocks.text: Audiobooks and podcasts

Prefer to listen instead of reading? No problem! Most of these books are available in audiobook format, making it easy to learn on the go — whether commuting, walking, or biohacking your sleep. And if you’re short on time, consider exploring the biohacking authors’podcasts, where they share the essence of their ideas in short, engaging formats. It’s a perfect way to stay informed and inspired without blocking out hours in your day.
To sum up
Biohacking optimizes human performance, health, and well-being by utilizing science, technology, and a deep understanding of human physiology and nutrition.

In this article, we explored many biohacking books, analyzing their key insights and categorizing them based on their suitability for beginners and advanced readers. From wellness tips to enhancing brain power, these books provide practical knowledge for improving health and optimizing body functions. Among the top biohacking books, “Lifespan” by David Sinclair stands out as the best biohacking book of 2026 due to its comprehensive exploration of aging and practical advice on how to slow it down.
